title: プロジェクトデザインⅢ(向井宏明研究室)
subtitle: Design Project III(Mukai Hiroaki)
educationalGoal: Based on the concrete knowledge of fundamental technologies, students acquire problem-solving skills related to computer & information engineering. Students are also given opportunities to experience R&D activities related to concrete information technology and systems. Through this process, students cultivate advanced abilities in the areas of problem setting, production process development, information gathering, communications, problem-solving in regional orientation, and making objective evaluations.
advice: Investigate and examine the relationships between the technologies and services of interest. Moreover, the following areas should be addressed. Students learn R&D methods through the development of programs or evaluation models. 1. Information infrastructure design, construction, evaluation and operation In this area, students focus on lifecycles, components, and the development process, tools and methods to solve issues, and so on. 2. Next-generation information infrastructure In this area, students explore content delivery by combining server, database, network, and program technologies, with the goals of creating reliable networks, collaborative work, and industry applications, etc. 3. Improving information system stability/disaster recovery Students will address topics such as redundancy, disaster recovery, non-functional design and so on. 4. Data structure analysis/conversion Students explore data structure analysis, processing, conversion with functions of programming languages such as Python3, Perl6, Elixir, Haskell, Kotlin, and Scala. 5. Application by cooperation among end users Systems that promote end user interaction, relationship extraction, SNS data aggregation, and so on, are examined.
requiredKnowledge: Research guidance policy In this laboratory, seminars by students and faculty members are conducted once a week. Students are expected to set themes, summarize survey analysis results, discover social problems, and conduct annual events such as the writing of academic papers and making conference presentations.

activityGoals.body: Be able to set one-year achievement goals in relation to your chosen research.
Be able to set a specific production approach based on your set research concept.
Be able to use your acquired information engineering expertise to advance your design and analysis efforts.
Be able to cope with various problems that occur during the design and analysis process.
Be able to technically describe what you have accomplished in a convincing manner.

achievementLevels.ideal: Be able to promote R&D activities smoothly according to the project plan (proposal) that you have created. In the results, it is desirable that students be able to announce concrete results that are scientifically and/or technically recognized as novel, effective, and reliable.
achievementLevels.standard: Be able to promote R&D activities smoothly according to the project plan (proposal) that you have created. In the results, it is desirable that students be able to announce concrete results that are based in scientific and technical reality.

lessons.content: Acquisition of knowledge and methods Students spread knowledge and improve technology among each other through discussions and observations of other students' activity reports.
lessons.assignments: Understand existing technologies, products, research, and methods, then organize purposes, functions, and effects. Students compare multiple items and clarify superiority based on evaluation viewpoints.

lessons.content: Improvement of students' ability Students create documents that are easy for others to understand and make progress on study items that were set based on the advice and suggestions of others. The deliverables can be software, system construction and documentation, and so on.
lessons.assignments: Refine management abilities such as those used in investigation, design, programming, system construction, evaluation method, progress management, and problem management.
